governing_spec.section: ## GOVERNANCE-JSON-ISOLATION-CORRECTIVE-001 — Close non-journal governance JSON store lost updates
governing_spec.finding: F09 · Governance JSON store 會遺失第二實例未看到的資料

two_instance_lost_update_prevention.implementation: services/governance/record_store.py: JsonGovernanceRecordStore upgraded with re-entrant POSIX file locking (_FileLock using fcntl.flock), fresh disk reload on read and write (_refresh()), and atomic file replacement (_save() with unique temporary file .tmp.<pid>.<uuid>, fsync, and os.replace). Multiple instances pointing to the same file coordinate safely without lost updates, including nested re-entrant scopes across independent store instances.

multiprocess_concurrency.implementation: services/governance/record_store.py: Independent OS processes writing distinct records concurrently coordinate via POSIX file locking on .<storage_name>.json.flock, preserving 100% of all distinct records without dropping or corrupting data.

insert_if_absent_duplicate_rejection.implementation: services/governance/record_store.py: insert_if_absent re-reads fresh state under file lock and in-process RLock, returning (True, record) for the winning insert and (False, canonical) for all concurrent or subsequent attempts with matching ID.

compare_and_set_version_conflict.implementation: services/governance/record_store.py: compare_and_set re-reads fresh state under file lock, verifying exact equality with expected_record before atomic write. Concurrent mutations with stale expected records fail closed, returning (False, current_record).

fresh_reads_across_instances.implementation: services/governance/record_store.py: get() and list_all() reload from disk under file lock via _coordinate(), ensuring writes from any process or instance are immediately observed by other long-lived instances without restart.

failed_write_restart_durability.implementation: services/governance/record_store.py: Atomic durable replacement using temporary file, os.fsync on file and parent directory, and os.replace. Pre-replacement filesystem errors during save restore in-memory state and preserve previous on-disk data without corruption. Post-replacement directory fsync errors raise without masking, while replaced bytes may already be visible on disk; durability remains unconfirmed without successful directory fsync. Readers never observe uncommitted state prior to replacement.

command_locks: store.lock() (POSIX file lock on .freeze_orders.json.flock + in-process store RLock)
store.lock() (POSIX file lock on .rollbacks.json.flock + in-process store RLock)

concurrency_control: insert_if_absent on creation (rejects duplicate decision_id with HTTP 409 conflict)
put_if_matches CAS on signatures/revocations (rejects concurrent mismatch with HTTP 409 conflict, enabling client retry from fresh state)
insert_if_absent idempotency (exact replay returns 200 with matching payload, duplicate mismatch returns HTTP 409 conflict)
consultation_handoffs.coverage_note: Consultation handoff HTTP route tests cover sequential operations, idempotent replays, security failures, and conflict rejection. Controlled multi-instance concurrent insertion semantics are verified by test_mounted_consumer_consultation_handoff_multi_instance.

ci_regression_fixed_permission_mode_on_r.finding: PR #5709 real Persona provisioning owner contracts CI (workflow 34304100683 / job 102317075569) at reviewed head d4d961804 failed 2/2 on the actual readonly-Docker-mount decision journal tests with PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied. Root cause: services/governance/record_store.py switched _save() from an ordinary write to tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile, whose backing file is always created mode 0600 regardless of umask; os.replace then published that restrictive mode verbatim as the canonical record file, narrowing an existing readable (0644) journal file to 0600 on its next write and breaking the distinct-UID readonly consumer relied on by the unchanged CI test. Base 15e2907b5 passed 2/2; head d4d961804 reproduced the same 2 failures locally against the actual pantheon-governance-contract:ci image with --read-only --cap-drop ALL mounts.
ci_regression_fixed_permission_mode_on_r.implementation: services/governance/record_store.py: added JsonGovernanceRecordStore._replacement_mode(), called via os.chmod(temporary_path, ...) immediately before os.replace() in _save(). When storage_path already exists, the temporary file is chmod'd to the existing file's exact current mode (stat.S_IMODE), so an established readable posture is never narrowed by a replace. When storage_path does not yet exist (first write), the temporary file is chmod'd to the umask-controlled default an ordinary open() would have produced (0o666 & ~current_umask), read via the standard os.umask(0)/os.umask(restore) probe. Unique temporary file creation, POSIX file locking, fsync of file and parent directory, and atomic os.replace are all unchanged.
ci_regression_fixed_permission_mode_on_r.regression_verification: Reverted only record_store.py to the exact HEAD (d4d961804) blob while keeping the two new tests: both new tests failed (AssertionError comparing 0600 vs the expected preserved/umask mode), confirming they reproduce the exact CI defect. Restoring the fix made all tests pass again. The two real readonly-Docker-mount tests, run against the unchanged pantheon-governance-contract:ci image with --read-only --cap-drop ALL --network none mounts, now pass (previously PermissionError).
